industry: Medical Devices / Specialty Nutrition + Pain Management
drawdown_context: AVNS is a 2014 Kimberly-Clark spin-off (formerly Halyard Health) selling Digestive Health products (MIC-KEY/Corpak/NeoMed enteral feeding) and Pain Management & Recovery products (ON-Q surgical pain pumps, Game Ready, COOLIEF/OrthogenRx/Trident RFA). FY24 net sales $687.8M (+2.2%) but Q4 2024 booked a $336.5M goodwill impairment plus a $100.2M HA-asset-group impairment after the stock had de-rated, driving a GAAP operating loss of $(396.2)M. Adjusted operating profit was actually +$87.3M (vs $79.7M FY23). The stock fell -48% to $12.75 at the 5/15/2025 cutoff. Senior leadership is unsettled: Michael Greiner (former CFO) became Interim CEO in October 2024 and signed the 10-K in that capacity; Warren Machan (former Kimberly-Clark Finance executive and consultant) became Interim CFO at the same time. By the Q1 2025 10-Q (filed 5/6/2025) a third officer Jason Pickett had become Interim CFO. Top-2 distributor concentration jumped from 28% (FY23) to 35% (FY24: McKesson 18% + Medline 17%). Q1 2025 segment reporting flipped from single segment (10-K) to two segments (Q1 10-Q). The Trump-2 tariff regime imposed in February-April 2025 hits AVNS's two Mexico manufacturing facilities (25% Mexico tariff), Canada manufacturing (10% global), and Chinese components (145%) directly. The forward +93% return reflects (a) a stock that had already absorbed the goodwill write-down at the cutoff, (b) demonstrable continued adjusted operating profitability, (c) a permanent CEO hire later in 2025, and (d) tariff fade.

rfm_tuples.R: We have served as the Company's auditor since 2013. /s/ Deloitte & Touche LLP, Atlanta, Georgia, February 26, 2025. [Two critical audit matters: (i) Net Sales / Accrued rebate expenses; (ii) Goodwill Valuation related to the $336.5M Q4 2024 impairment.] [Unqualified opinion on financial statements and on ICFR; no going-concern paragraph.]
rfm_tuples.f: Auditor history / change tracker. Test for resignations, restatements, ICFR adverse opinions, or Item 4.01 8-K events.
rfm_tuples.M_source: 10-K Report of Independent Registered Public Accounting Firm (PCAOB ID 34) + Item 9 (no changes/disagreements) + Item 9A (controls effective)
rfm_tuples.M_value: Deloitte & Touche LLP since 2013 (12-year tenure). Big 4. PCAOB ID 34. Unqualified opinion on financials and on ICFR. Item 9 reports NONE for changes/disagreements with accountants. Two CAMs: (1) Net Sales/Rebates (consistent for a distributor-heavy med device); (2) Goodwill Valuation -- exactly the area where AVNS just took $336.5M of impairment, but Deloitte signed off on the residual $455.6M without further write-down.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode A: Deloitte 12-year tenure with a clean opinion through a Q4 2024 goodwill triggering event is exactly the audit history a long-tier name should have. The Goodwill Valuation CAM is appropriate disclosure of the highest-judgment lever rather than evidence of audit friction. No 8-K Item 4.01 in the pre-cutoff window.

rfm_tuples.R: We expect our operating cash flow will be sufficient to meet our working capital requirements and fund capital expenditures in the next twelve months. [...] The Credit Agreement requires compliance with certain customary operational and financial covenants. As of December 31, 2024, we were in compliance with all of our debt covenants. [Cash and equivalents $107.7M; Term Loan outstanding $110.2M; Revolver $25M of $375M drawn; Credit Agreement matures June 24, 2027; effective interest rate 6.1%.]
rfm_tuples.f: Test runway claim against the actual Q1 2025 trajectory and against the June 2024 First Amendment to the Credit Agreement (filed as Exhibit 4.1 to Q3 2024 10-Q). If the amendment loosened covenants, it would be a tell; if it was housekeeping, it confirms the liquidity narrative.
rfm_tuples.M_source: Q1 2025 10-Q (accession 0001606498-25-000091, filed 2025-05-06) balance sheet + Q3 2024 10-Q (accession 0001606498-24-000084, filed 2024-10-30) Exhibit 4.1 reference
rfm_tuples.M_value: Q1 2025: cash declined modestly to $97.0M ($10.7M sequential decline) BUT total debt dropped from $134.7M to $107.4M (revolver paid down $25M, term loan paid down $2.3M). Net debt position improved to +$10.4M (debt > cash) vs $27.0M at year-end -- Q1 2025 cash from operations was +$25.7M, a clean reversal of the $(8.0)M Q1 2024 operating use. The June 26, 2024 First Amendment to the Credit Agreement was disclosed as an Exhibit but no covenant relief was announced in either the Q3 2024 10-Q or the 10-K (the company was in compliance at every measurement date). The amendment appears to have been administrative (lender re-alignment with JPM/MUFG/PNC/U.S. Bank as joint lead arrangers) rather than distressed.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode A: liquidity claim is confirmed by Q1 2025 trajectory -- operating cash flow turned positive, debt decreased, and the revolver is 93% undrawn ($350M of $375M capacity). The First Amendment was not a covenant break. Maturity is June 2027, well outside the cutoff window, and the $107.4M total debt is ~1.2x FY24 adjusted operating profit.

rfm_tuples.R: In 2024, sales to McKesson Corporation and Medline Industries accounted for approximately 18% and 17% of consolidated net sales, respectively. In the year ended December 31, 2023, sales to Medline Industries, McKesson Corporation, and Owens & Minor, Inc. accounted for approximately 15%, 13%, and 6% of consolidated net sales, respectively. [And: the Company has two customers accounting for >10% of accounts receivable in 2024 vs one in 2023.]
rfm_tuples.f: Customer concentration rate-of-change. Top-2-distributor combined exposure rose from 28% (FY23) to 35% (FY24) -- a 7-percentage-point absolute jump and a 25% relative jump in one year. Test whether this rising concentration is operationally explained or a structural risk.
rfm_tuples.M_value: FY22: Medline 12% + McKesson 12% + Owens & Minor 5% = 29%. FY23: Medline 15% + McKesson 13% + Owens & Minor 6% = 34%. FY24: McKesson 18% + Medline 17% = 35%. Order of the top two flipped (McKesson moved from #2 to #1). A/R concentration went from 'one customer' in 2023 to 'two customers' above 10% in 2024. The 10-K does not specifically name which two A/R customers, but the obvious inference is McKesson and Medline. With a single Specialty Nutrition Systems franchise driving most of the growth and most of the GPO contracts up for renegotiation on a 3-year cycle, the 35% concentration is now structural -- losing either name in a GPO bid cycle would be a Q-changing event.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode B: AVNS discloses each year's concentration accurately, but does not frame the trajectory (28% to 34% to 35%) as a risk. The Mode-B-relevant question is whether the concentration jump in 2024 is driven by hospital de-stocking through smaller distributors (which would be cyclical and reverse), or by GPO consolidation (which is structural). Given that McKesson, Medline, and O&M are the three dominant US med-distrib platforms, the concentration is essentially a function of GPO routing -- and AVNS now has 35% of sales through two counterparties whose 3-year GPO contracts are the binding renegotiation event.

rfm_tuples.R: Michael C. Greiner, age 52, was appointed Interim Chief Executive Officer in October 2024. Prior to such appointment, he had served as Senior Vice President and Chief Financial Officer since January 1, 2020. In January 2023, he had assumed the additional position of Chief Transformation Officer. [...] Warren J. Machan, age 59, was appointed as the Company's Interim Chief Financial Officer in October 2024. [...] Since 2021, Mr. Machan has served as a medical technology health care strategy consultant, primarily to the Company. [10-K signed Feb 26, 2025 by Greiner as Interim CEO and Machan as Interim CFO.]
rfm_tuples.f: C-suite stability -- time the CEO interim status against the goodwill impairment, the segment reorganization, and the executive severance multiplier change. Then check whether the interim status was resolved by the Q1 2025 10-Q signature page.
rfm_tuples.M_source: 10-K Item 10 (Executive Officers) + 10-K signatures + Q3 2024 10-Q signature page (Machan as Interim CFO) + Q1 2025 10-Q signature page (Pickett as Interim CFO)
rfm_tuples.M_value: Timeline: (i) October 2024 -- Greiner moves from CFO to Interim CEO; Machan (consultant since 2021, prior interim CFO in 2019) becomes Interim CFO. (ii) October 29, 2024 -- Compensation Committee raises Executive Severance Plan multiplier from 1.5x to 2.0x for all execs EXCEPT the CEO (Q3 2024 10-Q Item 5). (iii) November 1, 2024 -- Board authorizes a new $25M share repurchase program with a 10b5-1 plan. (iv) Q4 2024 -- Goodwill impairment of $336.5M plus HA asset impairment of $100.2M booked. (v) February 26, 2025 -- 10-K signed by Interim CEO Greiner and Interim CFO Machan. (vi) Q1 2025 -- CODM changes segment reporting from one to two segments. (vii) May 6, 2025 -- Q1 2025 10-Q signed by yet another Interim CFO (Jason M. Pickett, VP) -- NOT Machan. So in the seven months from October 2024 to May 2025, AVNS has had: 1 Interim CEO, 2 different Interim CFOs (Machan, Pickett), no permanent succession announced, the highest-risk goodwill test in company history, the largest impairment in company history, an executive severance bump for everyone-but-the-CEO, and a structural reorganization of segment reporting.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode B: any single one of these would be a yellow flag in isolation. The cluster -- interim CEO + two interim CFOs in 7 months + severance multiplier bump for non-CEOs + a $437M asset/goodwill write-down + a segment reorganization that disaggregates the previously-impaired reporting unit -- is the textbook 'lying-by-spreading' pattern. The 10-K's mention of Greiner as Interim CEO is buried in the Item 10 biography, never appears in the MD&A, and is not framed as a stress signal. The severance multiplier bump being routed through Item 5 of the Q3 2024 10-Q (rather than a stand-alone 8-K Item 5.02) is a classic disclosure-minimization tactic. AVNS is solvent, but the governance picture is exactly the kind that historically precedes either a strategic-review/sale or a 'permanent' CEO hire who marks down the residual goodwill in the next cycle.

rfm_tuples.R: In the fourth quarter of 2024, we revised downward our future projections for certain product lines due to lower net sales and future year margin expectations. This required us to assess the recoverability of a specific asset group during the fourth quarter of 2024, which resulted in an impairment loss of $100.2 million. Additionally, due to a decrease in our market capitalization, we determined it was more likely than not that the fair value of our medical devices reporting unit may be below its carrying value. Accordingly, we completed an interim goodwill impairment test as of December 1, 2024 and concluded that the fair value of the reporting unit was lower than its carrying value. As a result, during the fourth quarter of 2024, we recorded a $336.5 million impairment to goodwill. [Residual goodwill: $455.6M.]
rfm_tuples.f: Pressure-test the residual $455.6M goodwill cushion against the Q1 2025 interim goodwill test that was triggered by the segment reorganization. If both new segments pass the test, the residual is defensible; if either is close to the carrying-value line, the next impairment is in flight.
rfm_tuples.M_source: Q1 2025 10-Q Note 2 (Segment Information) + Q1 2025 10-Q Critical Accounting Policies
rfm_tuples.M_value: Q1 2025 10-Q discloses: 'In connection with the change in our reportable segment to two, we performed an interim goodwill impairment test as of January 1, 2025, and determined that the fair values of our reporting units exceeded the net carrying amounts. However, there can be no assurance that the assumptions and estimates made for purposes of the annual goodwill impairment test will prove to be accurate. Volatility in the equity and debt markets, or increases in interest rates, could result in a higher discount rate. Changes in sales volumes, selling prices and costs of goods sold, the effect of new or higher tariffs or increases in interest rates could cause changes in our forecasted cash flows.' Goodwill split at 3/31/2025: SNS $327.6M (the growth franchise -- passes easily), PM&R $128.0M (the de-rated franchise -- closer to the line). The Q1 test cushion percentages are NOT disclosed in the 10-Q, which is the highest-discrimination tell: when a company passes a goodwill test comfortably it usually quantifies the cushion; AVNS does not.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode B: re-segmenting the business right after impairing the single reporting unit allocates $327.6M of goodwill to the growth franchise (SNS, +6.9% Q1) and $128.0M to the deteriorating one (PM&R, -0.2% Q1). The 10-Q's failure to disclose the post-test cushion percentage for either reporting unit is the kind of omission the framework flags -- if the PM&R cushion were 40%+, management would quantify; the silence implies the cushion is thinner. With tariffs now explicitly cited as a goodwill-impairment risk factor in the Q1 10-Q, a second impairment in 2025 on PM&R is plausible, although smaller in magnitude than the Q4 2024 charge.

rfm_tuples.R: Most of our manufacturing facilities are located outside the United States in Mexico. [...] On February 1, 2025, President Donald Trump announced the imposition of a 25% tariff on all goods imported from Mexico. Days later, President Trump suspended the imposition of such tariffs for a period of 30 days. As of the date of this Form 10-K, it remains unclear whether new tariffs will be imposed on goods imported from Mexico and, if so, at what level and for how long. [10-K filed 2/26/2025.]
rfm_tuples.f: Time the 10-K tariff-risk disclosure (filed 2/26/2025) against the Q1 2025 10-Q (filed 5/6/2025) to test whether the post-cutoff tariff escalation matches the 10-K's bracketed scenario. Quantify the exposure: AVNS has two Mexico plants (per the 10-K Item 2 Properties and Risk Factor), Canadian manufacturing, and Chinese-sourced components.
rfm_tuples.M_source: Q1 2025 10-Q Part II Item 1A Risk Factors (the only updated risk factor)
rfm_tuples.M_value: Q1 10-Q (5/6/2025) escalates the tariff narrative substantially: 'Since February 2025, the United States has imposed a number of new tariffs on goods originating from many countries in the world, including: (i) tariffs totaling 145% on Chinese-origin goods; (ii) a 25% tariff on Mexican-origin goods; (iii) a 10% global tariff imposed on the entire world, including Korean-origin goods (which affects imports of certain of our products from Canada); and (iv) reciprocal tariffs on goods from most of the countries in the world, which reciprocal tariffs have been paused through mid-July 2025...' AVNS does NOT quantify the bps margin impact in the 10-Q. With ~$246.7M of cost of goods sold in FY24 and the bulk of manufacturing in Mexico, a 25% Mexico tariff (un-mitigated) implies $50M+ of annualized cost pressure -- roughly 60% of FY24 adjusted operating profit. Mitigations are 'we are taking steps' (i.e., not quantified).
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode B: the 10-K (2/26/2025) acknowledged the 25% Mexico tariff threat and the 30-day pause. The Q1 10-Q (5/6/2025) confirmed the scenario escalated to a multi-front tariff war but provided no margin-impact quantification. Both filings rely on 'we are exploring options' / 'we are taking steps' -- language that has no Mode A anchor. For a medical-device company that just took a $437M impairment and revised projections downward on the basis of margin compression, an additional un-quantified 25% Mexico cost layer on top of a 145% China component layer is exactly the kind of materially-adverse exposure that the framework's underwriting-risk-vs-quantification test catches. The market did not punish this further (the +93% forward return tells you tariffs eventually faded), but at the cutoff date the disclosure was deliberately bracketed.

rfm_tuples.R: [10-K reports single reportable segment: 'We operate in one reportable segment which is the manufacturing and marketing of our portfolio of medical devices.' Q4 2024 goodwill test was on this single 'medical devices reporting unit' which resulted in the $336.5M impairment.] [Q1 2025 10-Q: 'During the first quarter of 2025, our CODM began managing the business at a disaggregated level beyond our previously defined medical devices segment. Accordingly, we conduct our business in two operating and reportable segments. Prior year amounts have been reclassified to conform with the current year presentation.']
rfm_tuples.f: Claim evolution between 10-K (one segment) and Q1 2025 10-Q (two segments). Test whether the segment reorganization is a substantive change in how management runs the business or a goodwill-allocation maneuver to protect the residual $455.6M from a second impairment.
rfm_tuples.M_source: 10-K Note 21 Segment Reporting (single segment) + Q1 2025 10-Q Note 2 Segment Information (two segments, retrospective reclassification)
rfm_tuples.M_value: The single-segment goodwill test on 12/1/2024 took $336.5M out at the consolidated reporting-unit level -- a maximum-cushion-erosion test. Within ~4 weeks of that test (on 1/1/2025, per the Q1 10-Q) the CODM 'began managing the business at a disaggregated level' and split goodwill into SNS $327.6M and PM&R $128.0M, then ran a new test that passed for both new reporting units. The 10-K's Q4 2024 disclosure does NOT mention any pending segment reorganization (no 'subsequent events' note for the segment change, which would normally be disclosed since the 10-K filed 2/26/2025 was AFTER the CODM-change date of 1/1/2025). The timing is mechanically perfect: take the impairment on the single segment first (maximize the cushion-erosion test), then reorganize and re-test on the new structure (gives both reporting units a fresh cushion).
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode B (claim evolution, the framework's strongest tell): a CODM that 'began managing the business at a disaggregated level' on 1/1/2025 must have started thinking about that change before 12/1/2024 (the impairment test date). The 10-K filed 2/26/2025 should have disclosed the upcoming segment change as a subsequent event under ASC 855, but does not. The order-of-operations -- impair single segment 12/1/24, change CODM 1/1/25, sign 10-K 2/26/25 silent on segment change, re-test goodwill on new segments in Q1 -- is the kind of accounting choreography that gives both new reporting units a fresh impairment cushion just months after the historical reporting unit failed its own test. This is not necessarily fraud (the new segments may legitimately reflect how the business is run), but it is the kind of disclosure-asymmetry the framework targets.

rfm_tuples.R: On November 1, 2024, the Board of Directors approved a new one-year program under which we may repurchase up to $25.0 million of our common stock. [...] We have established a pre-arranged trading plan under Rule 10b5-1 of the Exchange Act in connection with this share repurchase program. [Prior $25M program approved July 28, 2023 was fully utilized by Q2 2024 at higher prices.]
rfm_tuples.f: Capital allocation timing -- was the November 1, 2024 buyback authorization a response to the depressed share price (i.e., buying back into the de-rating), or was it formulaic? Time it against the Interim CEO appointment (October 2024) and the Q4 goodwill impairment.
rfm_tuples.M_source: 10-K Item 5 Market for Registrant's Common Equity + 10-K Note 19 Share Repurchase Program + Q1 2025 10-Q balance sheet
rfm_tuples.M_value: Sequence: October 2024 -- Interim CEO/CFO appointments. October 29, 2024 -- severance multiplier bump for non-CEOs. November 1, 2024 -- new $25M buyback authorized with a 10b5-1 plan. Q4 2024 -- $336.5M goodwill impairment + $100.2M HA impairment. Q1 2025 -- Treasury Stock balance per Q1 10-Q balance sheet did not change between Q4 2024 and Q1 2025 (no new shares repurchased in Q1 2025). The 10b5-1 plan was set up immediately before the Q4 goodwill write-down, which is consistent with Rule 10b5-1's safe harbor (set up plan when not in possession of MNPI), but the timing -- three days before the announcement of the impairment study being underway -- is the kind of insider-action-vs-calendar pattern the framework flags. The 10-K does not disclose how much, if any, has been repurchased under the November 1 plan.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode B: a fresh $25M buyback authorization four days before announcing the largest goodwill triggering event in company history, set up under a 10b5-1 plan that gives the Company plausible deniability for MNPI, is exactly the kind of capital-action timing the framework's insider_vs_calendar detector should pick up. The fact that no shares were actually purchased under the new plan in Q1 2025 (treasury stock balance flat) suggests the plan was set up as optionality, not executed -- which is consistent with management thinking the stock would go lower and waiting to deploy. The cleanliness of the 10b5-1 paperwork is a Mode A pass; the Mode B reading is that the plan timing was designed to give the Company maximum optionality across a goodwill impairment that management knew was coming.

rfm_tuples.R: [10-K Item 9A: Disclosure Controls and Procedures were operating effectively as of December 31, 2024. /s/ Deloitte & Touche LLP -- unqualified ICFR opinion.] [And: 'On July 6, 2021, we entered into a Deferred Prosecution Agreement (the DPA) with the DOJ that resolved their criminal investigation related to our MicroCool surgical gowns. Pursuant to the terms of the DPA, in July 2021 the Company made a payment of $22.2 million. The DPA term expired on July 7, 2024 and in January 2025, the United States District Court for the Northern District of Texas dismissed the DOJ's case against the Company.']
rfm_tuples.f: Legal-recidivism check. AVNS has a DPA history (MicroCool surgical gown criminal investigation 2015-2021, $22.2M paid). The DPA expired 7/7/2024 and was dismissed 1/2025. Test whether any new criminal-investigation tells, qui tam unsealings, or FDA warning letters appeared in the pre-cutoff window.
rfm_tuples.M_source: 10-K Note 14 Commitments and Contingencies + Q3 2024 10-Q + Q1 2025 10-Q legal proceedings
rfm_tuples.M_value: 10-K (Note 14) discloses ONLY the DPA dismissal (positive event, January 2025). No new qui tam complaints, no new DOJ subpoenas, no FDA warning letters, no recall disclosures in the 10-K or the Q1 2025 10-Q. The Q1 2025 10-Q Item 1 Legal Proceedings has the boilerplate language with no specific case carve-outs. The RH Divestiture (10/2/2023) removed the surgical gown / respiratory product lines that were the basis of the DPA from the business entirely, so the recidivism risk is structurally lower than at the time of the DPA. Indemnification: AVNS is responsible for spin-off-era legal liabilities under the Kimberly-Clark distribution agreement, but FY24 indemnification spend was $0.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode A: legal/regulatory ledger is genuinely clean at the cutoff. The DPA dismissal in January 2025 (one month before the 10-K filing) is a tangible Mode A pass -- the DOJ had four years to find recidivism and did not. The RH Divestiture in October 2023 also removed the product line that was the basis of the criminal investigation, structurally de-risking the legal book. This is a real differentiator from a typical 'lying-about-distress' framework target -- AVNS does not have a recidivist FCA / DOJ pattern.

rfm_tuples.R: [10-K Adjusted Operating Profit (non-GAAP): FY24 $87.3M vs FY23 $79.7M vs FY22 $73.2M -- 'On a GAAP basis, we had an operating loss compared to operating income in the prior year, primarily due to goodwill and intangibles impairment and plant separation costs, partially offset by higher sales and lower selling costs.'] [And: Q1 2025 Adjusted Operating Income (non-GAAP) $17.1M vs $16.3M Q1 2024 -- modest growth.]
rfm_tuples.f: Test whether the underlying business is genuinely growing (Mode A) or whether the adjusted-operating-profit growth is achieved by progressively widening the add-back schedule. Decompose the FY23-to-FY24 adjusted operating profit bridge.
rfm_tuples.M_source: 10-K Item 7 MD&A non-GAAP reconciliation + Q1 2025 10-Q MD&A non-GAAP reconciliation
rfm_tuples.M_value: FY24 to FY23 adjusted operating profit bridge: $87.3M vs $79.7M = +$7.6M (+9.5%) growth. Add-backs FY24: acquisition $4.2M + restructuring $(0.8)M + post-RH transition $3.1M + post-RH restructuring $8.9M + impairment $436.7M + EU MDR $6.2M + amortization $25.2M = $483.5M. Add-backs FY23: $3.3M + $28.2M + $0 + $0 + $6.0M + $3.7M + $10.0M legal + $24.3M = $75.5M. The dominant FY24 add-back is the $436.7M impairment -- i.e., real cash-equivalent costs ex-impairment (acquisition, restructuring, post-RH cleanup, EU MDR, amortization) are $46.8M FY24 vs $75.5M FY23 -- a $28.7M improvement that is plausibly real cost discipline. Adjusted operating profit margin is 12.7% FY24 vs 11.8% FY23 -- a 90 bps real expansion. Q1 2025 adjusted operating income $17.1M vs $16.3M = +5% YoY on +0.8% revenue, indicating modest operating leverage. Revenue growth on a clean basis was Digestive Health +6.7% (the growth franchise) offsetting Pain Management -3.4%.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode A: AVNS is genuinely a mid-single-digit-revenue-growth, low-double-digit-adjusted-operating-margin business that just absorbed a stock-de-rating-triggered $437M non-cash impairment. The underlying operating performance is consistent with the narrative. The Digestive Health franchise (now SNS) is +6.7% on volume +5%+ and is the actual driver. This is the Mode A pass that, in combination with the C-suite cluster and the segment-reorganization choreography, defines AVNS as a 'honest-but-stressed' name rather than a 'lying-about-distress' name -- exactly the kind of control_survivor that the framework should NOT flag as SHORT-tier on the operating-business test.

summary: AVNS is a borderline case: deterministic Mode-A scanners return CLEAN (Deloitte Big-4 since 2013, no going-concern, $350M undrawn revolver maturing 2027, adjusted operating profit growing $73M->$80M->$87M FY22-24 with +5% Q1 2025 YoY, durable SNS franchise +6.7%/+6.9%, DPA dismissed January 2025, no qui tam / FCA / FDA tells, RH Divestiture having structurally removed the criminal-investigation product line). The Mode-B cluster, however, is unusually dense for a control_survivor: (1) Interim CEO since October 2024 (the former CFO) PLUS two different Interim CFOs in seven months (Machan signed the 10-K, Pickett signed the Q1 10-Q) -- no permanent succession announced at the cutoff. (2) Non-CEO executive severance multiplier bumped 1.5x->2.0x on Oct 29 2024, disclosed via Q3 10-Q Item 5 rather than a stand-alone 8-K -- three days before a new $25M 10b5-1 buyback authorization and ~30 days before the goodwill triggering event. (3) Single-segment 10-K impaired $336.5M of goodwill on 12/1/2024; the CODM 'began managing the business at a disaggregated level' on 1/1/2025; the 10-K (filed 2/26/2025) failed to disclose the imminent segment change as an ASC 855 subsequent event; the Q1 10-Q's interim goodwill test on the new SNS + PM&R reporting units passed without disclosed cushion percentages -- a textbook claim-evolution / accounting-choreography pattern. (4) $437M Q4 2024 non-cash impairment was triggered by 'a decrease in our market capitalization' rather than by explicit operational deterioration -- the company is letting the stock price drive the writedown rather than naming the operating tells. (5) Distributor concentration crept from 24% (FY22) to 28% (FY23) to 35% (FY24: McKesson 18% + Medline 17%) without being framed as a structural risk. (6) Both Mexico manufacturing plants directly exposed to the Trump-2 25% Mexico tariff (plus 145% China, 10% global), with no quantified margin impact. Severities: 4 PASS / 3 MODERATE / 3 SEVERE / 0 RED -> mechanical composite 0.90 (SHORT-tier). Given the strong Mode-A pass cluster (audit, liquidity, legal, underlying operations) and the realized +93% forward return, AVNS is a known limitation of the framework: a control_survivor whose disclosure pattern around interim leadership + goodwill choreography + tariff handwaving genuinely deserves the SEVERE flags even though the business itself is healthy and the post-cutoff outcome was positive. The framework correctly identifies the disclosure-pattern weakness but mis-prices the operating-business value; an investor reading both the rfm_tuples severities AND the mode_a_pass_cluster should under-weight the SHORT-tier signal here.
